title: Limiting Options: Beat competitors by shrinking their choices, not growing yours
summary: Jason Cohen takes the winning Othello AI strategy (minimize the opponent's legal moves) and applies it to competitive strategy. Rather than only maximizing your own position, force competitors into low-percentage, expensive paths via exclusive deals, overpaying for top ad slots, and owning the "expert" position in your market.

principles.text: Limiting a competitor's choices matters more than which choices they have.
principles.quote: Limiting choice is more important than what the choices are.

principles.text: Ask how to push competitors into low-percentage or expensive options, costing them money, luck or creativity.
principles.quote: How can you limit their choices to things that are low-percentage or expensive?** Make them have to spend more money, get more lucky, or be more creative.

principles.text: Honoring competitors' coupons removes coupons as a way for them to beat you.
principles.quote: This eliminates the coupon as a way for your competitor to "beat" you; coupons are no longer a "choice" to develop a competitive edge.

principles.text: Overpay for the best ad slots: the value includes forcing rivals into low-converting positions, not just direct ROI.
principles.quote: You are paying too much if you measure the direct ROI only, but there's also the value of forcing competitors into a low-converting ad position, leading to many fewer customers at any price.

principles.text: Lock up exclusive deals with the largest affiliates so competitors are left with affiliates generating far fewer leads.
principles.quote: You are (again) paying too much if you measure the direct ROI only, but you force competitors to work with affiliates who can generate only 1/10th the leads.

principles.text: Become 'the expert' in your category so claiming that position is too expensive for rivals, especially when selling to Enterprise.
principles.quote: we're so strongly established as "the experts in code review," it would take an expensive, time-consuming effort for someone else to claim par, much less surpass what we've done.
